parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/users/domain/user.ts sits in the domain layer, but it does more than model the User entity. It also does infrastructure and presentation work. (1) When the module loads, it calls databaseConfig() and checks isDocumentDatabase to choose the id type. That ties the domain model to which persistence backend is configured, which is infrastructure configuration logic. (2) Every field has @ApiProperty decorators from @nestjs/swagger, with examples and types. That is API documentation and transport schema work, which belongs to presentation. (3) The @Expose({ groups: ['me', 'admin'] }) and @Exclude({ toPlainOnly: true }) decorators from class-transformer decide how the entity is serialized for HTTP responses and which fields each role can see. That is response shaping, also a presentation concern. Because of these, the file does not match the role of the domain layer.
